walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed Penicillium mould killing bacteria.

He couldn't make enough to test on people. In 1941 Florey and Chain mass-produced it. US factories scaled up by D-Day 1944, saving thousands of Allied lives.

The 1942 Beveridge Report attacked five giants including disease.

Labour's Aneurin Bevan launched the NHS on 5 July 1948 — free at the point of use, paid for by tax. It was the world's first fully nationalised health service.

In 1953 Watson and Crick described the DNA double helix.

Keyhole surgery, MRI scanners and the Human Genome Project (2003) followed. Lifestyle diseases — cancer, heart disease, diabetes — became the new battlefront. Anti-smoking laws came in 2007.
